analysis.title: NVIDIA Corporation: "We've got this": Confident, reassuring call; compelling valuation
key_insights: BofA reiterates Buy on NVDA with a $280 price objective against a $155.46 share price after the fiscal Q3 FY27 print (reported 11/18/2026). It calls the earnings call very reassuring under Interim CEO Colette Kress, while saying it may be premature to sound the all-clear.

Company guidance for FY28 (CY27) revenue growth was raised to about 75% YoY from about 70%, off a higher 2H FY27 base. Management says both demand and supply improved. NVDA is still studying the new export controls.

Fiscal Q3 revenue was $115.8bn (+20% QoQ, +103% YoY), 6.1% above Street ($109.2bn) and above the $108bn +/-2% guide. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.68 against Street $2.47. Non-GAAP gross margin was 74.9% against 74.0% Street, driven by mix.

Fiscal Q4 guide is $130bn +/-3% with no licensed Hopper China sales included, about 4.1% above Street ($124.9bn). Q4 has an extra week, and BofA estimates the guide implies only about +4% QoQ after adjusting for it. Q4 gross margin guide is 71-72%, which management calls the bottom, with 72-73% expected in FY28.

Capital returns were a record $28bn in the quarter ($22bn buybacks, $6bn dividends). The buyback authorization was raised by $150bn, leaving $227bn to use by end-FY28. NVDA now plans to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses, versus the June framing of 50% or more.

Board chair Harvey Jones said the board unanimously accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO and does not intend to reinstate him. Colette Kress is Interim CEO and an external and internal search is underway and will not be rushed. The board also set up a national security and export control oversight committee to engage the US government.

Vera Rubin shipped nearly $20bn (about 17% of revenue) in its first production quarter, NVDA's fastest ramp. Hyperscalers put it into production in about a month, half the time of Grace Blackwell. Rubin Ultra is on track for next year and Feynman for 2028.

Data Center revenue was $107.6bn (+21% QoQ, +110% YoY) with Hyperscale at $60.1bn (14% above Street) and AI Clouds, Industrial, Enterprise at $47.5bn (3.3% below Street). Networking was more than $21bn versus $8.2bn a year ago.

Demand signals cited on the call: compute is fully utilized at every hyperscaler and neocloud, older GPUs recontracted at up to 2x original price, B300 rental rates are up more than 60% since launch, and token prices are down about 60% since May. Cloud industry backlog is about $2.5tn, up from $2tn three months ago.
Licensed Hopper sales to China were $2.4bn (about 2% of revenue). Shipments have stopped and the Q4 guide includes none. New export controls came out this week.

Balance sheet and commitment disclosures: purchase commitments of $390bn, lease and cloud commitments a little over $100bn, neocloud commitments of $32bn, and $105bn of credit support for the PORTS-Pike campus. NVDA is now rigorously evaluating new commitments. Inventory rose to $39.7bn (124 days) and net cash fell 1.0% QoQ to $65.4bn.

BofA raises FY27/28/29E sales by +5%/+8%/+0% and EPS by +6%/+9%/unch to $9.62/$17.17/$23.17. The price objective now uses 16x CY27E PE (vs. 18x prior), citing the recent sector multiple re-rating and CEO transition risk.

BofA argues valuation is at a generational low, under 10x forward PE against a 30x median, and that a normal environment would price the stock near its 30-35% EPS growth CAGR for CY26-30E. Even a bear case of flat CY28 sales yields about $16 EPS, or 9.7x PE at $155.
Longer-term, BofA models EPS power of about $30 by CY30E, assuming AI data center share falls to 50% from about 65% currently, offset by cost controls and buybacks.

Risks flagged: delayed 10-Q filing, a CEO transition that could take time, neocloud funding and China scrutiny, headline and financial risk from the ex-CEO's departure and government scrutiny, rising memory costs and custom-chip competition pressuring gross margin, and supplier commitments becoming a burden if growth fails to materialize.

market_movers.rationale: BofA reiterates Buy and a $280 price objective, now based on 16x CY27E PE versus 18x prior. It argues sub-10x forward PE is unwarranted given 30-35% EPS growth and raised FY28 guidance.

sector_views.rationale: BofA sees about $2.2tn AI data center systems TAM by CY30E with NVDA holding roughly 50% or more share, supporting EPS power of $30+ by CY30E.

earnings_insights: Fiscal Q3 FY27 (Oct-26) reported 11/18/2026: revenue $115.8bn reported, vs Street consensus $109.2bn and BofA estimate $108.1bn. Non-GAAP EPS including options $2.68 reported, vs Street consensus $2.47, BofA estimate $2.45 and buyside bogey about $2.65.
Fiscal Q3 reported non-GAAP gross margin 74.9% vs Street consensus 74.0%. Non-GAAP opex $8.84bn reported vs $9.0bn company guide. Non-GAAP operating margin 67.2% reported vs Street consensus 66.0%.

Fiscal Q4 FY27 company guidance (not yet reported): revenue $130bn +/-3%, gross margin 71-72%, non-GAAP opex about $10.7bn. Street consensus before the guide was revenue $124.9bn and EPS $2.75. New BofA Q4 EPS estimate is $2.86 vs prior BofA $2.56.

BofA estimates (forecast): FY27E EPS $9.62, FY28E $17.17, FY29E $23.17. Consensus EPS (Bloomberg) is $9.33 for FY27E and $15.84 for FY28E. Consensus (Visible Alpha) is $9.69, $16.47 and $23.31 for FY27E to FY29E.
Company guidance for FY28 revenue growth is about 75% YoY, up from about 70%. BofA models FY28E sales of $741.4bn and FY29E of $955.2bn (+28.8%).

Segment reported vs Street for fiscal Q3: Data Center $107.6bn vs $102.0bn, Hyperscale $60.1bn vs $52.6bn, AI Clouds, Industrial, Enterprise $47.5bn vs $49.1bn, Networking $21.1bn vs $20.0bn, Edge Computing $8.2bn vs $7.5bn.

trade_ideas.description: Long NVDA equity, Buy rating, $280 price objective
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuation under 10x CY27E PE and a raised FY28 growth outlook of about 75% make risk-reward the most compelling across BofA's coverage.
trade_ideas.risk: Ex-CEO government scrutiny, AI capex and data center buildout uncertainty, export restrictions, memory costs and custom-chip competition.

risk_factors: CEO transition could take time. A permanent CEO has not been named.
Headline and financial risk from the ex-CEO's departure and increased US government scrutiny, including scrutiny of NVDA's dominant position in AI chips.
Neocloud funding risk and higher scrutiny of riskier neocloud shipments. NVDA carries $32bn of neocloud commitments and $105bn of credit support for the PORTS-Pike campus.
Incremental export restrictions on high-end AI products overseas, with China shipments already stopped.
Rising memory costs and custom-chip (ASIC) competition could pressure gross margin. Kress gave no long-term pricing commitment in response to the ASIC question.
Supplier purchase commitments of $390bn could become a burden if growth fails to materialize.
AI capex and data center buildouts remain in flux.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 shows a CY28 scenario analysis: bear case (sales flat YoY, gross margin 65.0%) EPS of ~$16 or ~10x PE at $155, base case $23.17 or 6.7x, and bull case (sales up 10% in the scenario text) EPS of ~$27 or ~6x PE.
Exhibit 4 compares NVDA with other Mag-7/Tech-10 names, showing NVDA at ~0.1x PEG versus an ex-NVDA average of 1.7x and about 50% FCF margin versus under 12% for others.
vol_and_positioning: BofA notes NVDA trades at about 10.2x CY27E PE versus a non-NVDA Mag-7/Tech-10 median of 17.4x, and at about 0.1x PEG versus an average of 1.7x for the group.
The stock sits near the low end of its 52-week range of $148.80 to $243.37, at $155.46.
geopolitical: New US export controls on high-end AI products came out the week of the earnings call, and NVDA is still studying them. The Q4 guide excludes licensed Hopper data center sales to China.
The board created a national security and export control oversight committee to improve engagement with US government agencies, following US government scrutiny tied to the ex-CEO.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA says NVDA trades under 10x CY27E PE versus a 30x median despite 30-35% EPS CAGR for CY26-30E, FY28 growth guidance raised to about 75%, and a bear case that still yields about $16 EPS in CY28.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA lists ex-CEO government scrutiny, a CEO transition that could take time, delayed 10-Q, neocloud funding risk, export restrictions, memory cost and custom-chip pressure on gross margin, and $390bn of supplier commitments if growth fails to materialize.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth failing to materialize against supplier commitments, or incremental export restrictions and ex-CEO scrutiny escalating. The report names no specific price or print level.

theme_stances.key_argument: Kress said it is business as usual and customers and suppliers are supportive, but the CEO transition could take time and carries headline risk.
